title: Confidential-GPU attestation lands as a cloud-AI contract term by Q2 2027
body: Apple's decision to run Private Cloud Compute on Google Cloud, with Apple Foundation Model inference executing on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs in confidential-computing mode, is the first time a frontier vendor has placed its private inference onto a rival cloud's silicon while keeping the trust boundary. The deal works only because the hardware can prove itself: remote attestation on genuine, untampered GPUs, a cryptographic ledger of every node in the fleet, public binary inspection, and a security bounty extended to the hosted nodes. The prediction is that this stops being an Apple-specific engineering feat and becomes a procurement primitive. Within the next year, expect at least one more frontier-vendor or hyperscaler inference arrangement to name remote GPU attestation, confidential-computing mode, and a verifiable node ledger as contracted, auditable terms rather than marketing claims. That turns confidential-compute hardware from a security feature into a commercial gate on where private AI inference is allowed to run, pulling chip vendors, clouds, and model providers into a shared attestation standard.
